title: Help developers understand focusable areas and links

labels.name: needs implementer interest
labels.description: Moving the issue forward requires implementers to express interest

body:
### What problem are you trying to solve? When websites implement links that navigate to sections of content—whether on the same page or another—they often omit the tabindex="-1" attribute from the target content. Without this attribute, non-interactive elements fail to receive proper focus, preventing certain assistive technologies from moving to the intended content. **Problematic example** ``` Learn about us ...

About Us

``` While developers bear responsibility for addressing this issue, as the HTML specification on focusable areas has been established for some time, the specification could better emphasize the relationship between this feature and hyperlinks. Assistive technologies impacted by the lack of focusable content include: * Windows Screen Magnifier with Keyboard Focus tracking turned on: The viewport resets to the top-left corner. * JAWS 2023 & Chrome 124: The page structure is re-announced starting with the page title, although the virtual cursor is corrected. * iOS 18.3.2 & 17.4 VoiceOver & Safari: Focus is reset to the top of the page. * iOS 17.4 Full Keyboard Access turned on, external keyboard & Safari: Focus is reset to the top of the page. ### What solutions exist today? Adding the `tabindex="-1"` attribute is a simple solution for developers, yet many may not realize its necessity. I believe this stems from a misunderstanding dating back to 2016, [when Google suggested](https://developer.chrome.com/blog/focus-start-point) that this attribute was only required for sequential focus navigation and could otherwise be omitted. **Accessible example** ``` Learn about us ...

About Us

``` ### How would you solve it? I would try to add a note somewhere useful and visible that helps developers understand the need for this attribute, although I admit that I do not know where this should be. ### Anything else? Some demonstrations can be found on my codepen (WIP): https://codepen.io/Tab-able/full/dPPPONR
